solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: European PM having a pop at philosophy, briefly

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word for the philosophy loses its last letter

parts.note: Taoism, the Chinese philosophy, without its final letter
'five pounds a pop' means five pounds each

explanation.surface: A European prime minister takes a quick swipe at philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taoiseach is the prime minister of Ireland; 'a pop' is the informal 'apiece'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoiseach is the Irish title for the head of the government of Ireland, a European country.

clue.text: Old Bill — or what it is now?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for the police
second meaning: a parliamentary bill from long ago has since been passed into statute

explanation.surface: A wry question about what has become of the old police force.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Bill is British slang for the police; read literally, an old bill that was passed is now part of the legal code.
explanation.definitionFit: The police are colloquially called the law, and an enacted bill becomes binding legislation.

clue.text: 10 up for disorder, but finally case dismissed at the end of the day?

definitions.text: case dismissed at the end of the day

indicators.note: put up for disorder, the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, EAT INTO
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word but

parts.note: the last letter of but

explanation.surface: A court case dismissed at the end of the day after some disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case dismissed' sounds legal, but a case here is a medical patient sent home the same day.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpatient is a hospital case treated without an overnight stay, so sent home by evening.

clue.text: Hazard guess finally, with some reflecting

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word guess

parts.note: last letter of guess
with and and both mean together with

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: some of something is part of it

explanation.surface: A risky guess is made, with some people reflecting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazard is a golf term for an obstacle on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a bunker filled with sand is one of the hazards a player must avoid.

clue.text: Mafia muscle holds up deadly weapon

indicators.note: one thing holds another by having it inside

parts.note: ab is short for an abdominal muscle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Mafia is called the mob

explanation.surface: A Mafia heavy holds up someone with a deadly weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mafia muscle' reads as one thug, but the two words split: the mob and a stomach muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic bomb is a nuclear weapon of devastating lethal power.

clue.text: Gathered there's a DVD shortly for release

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the disc abbreviation goes
letters set loose for release can fall into any order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
DVD with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A film is gathered up, as a DVD is about to come out.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvested crops have been gathered in, so both words mean collected.

clue.text: Royal award back in '91 for rousing chiller

indicators.note: back means the royal award's letters are read the other way
rousing means rising up, which in a down clue reads the year from the bottom
one piece goes in the other

parts.note: 91 in Roman numerals
Order of the British Empire, an honour given by the monarch

explanation.surface: A royal honour handed back in 1991 makes for a stirring thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour; '91 is turned into Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is a cooler or refrigerator, something that keeps food chilled.

clue.text: I'm obliged to avoid capture

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep away from it, so those letters stay out

parts.note: capture and taking both mean seizing
ta is British informal for thanks, much obliged

explanation.surface: Someone declares they must steer clear of being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the thanks from the taking leaves the piece; read whole, the clue is the chess piece speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the king is the one piece that may never be left where it could be taken.

clue.text: I craft something witty

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a liner is a seagoing craft

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of composing a clever remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a short joke or quip delivered in a single sentence.

clue.text: Where lots go, after warning to move about

indicators.note: letters that move about change places with one another

parts.note: a caution is a warning

explanation.surface: Lots of people go somewhere after being warned to circulate.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots are the items offered for sale at an auction, where bidders compete.

clue.text: Use up to ten: aim for reduction, somehow

indicators.note: reduction means a cut, so the word aim loses its last letter
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
aim shortened

explanation.surface: Instructions to spend up to ten while aiming to cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into savings is to consume or deplete part of them.

clue.text: Roll back voluble Franglais speaker's gift?

indicators.note: going back, the phrase is read from its end towards its start

parts.note: a talker has the gift of the gab; in Franglais, mixing French and English, that is le gab

explanation.surface: Someone rolls out the talent of a chatty speaker of mixed French and English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' looks like a verb; it is a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled and then baked.

clue.text: As an all-rounder, returning towel, bat, pad and gloves

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the enclosed letters are read right to left
gloves is a verb here: the list encloses the answer as a glove encloses a hand

parts.note: the letters running from the end of towel into the start of and

explanation.surface: A cricket all-rounder's kit list: towel, bat, pad and gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone versatile who can turn their hand to anything is adaptable, as an all-rounder is.

clue.text: Square peg on cross put in wrong

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the peg goes second

parts.note: X is a cross
a tee is a golfer's peg

explanation.surface: A square peg put in the wrong hole, with an angry cross.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'peg on cross' puts the tee after the X.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixteen is a square number, four times four.

clue.text: Get to English class with dead snake?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer living
an asp is a snake
E is short for English
a rate is a class, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Reaching English class carrying a dead snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to' reads as arriving, but it means annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gets to you irritates you, and to exasperate is to irritate intensely.

clue.text: Behind award for cycling?

indicators.note: cycling round moves the last letter of the award to the front

parts.note: a British Academy film or television award

explanation.surface: Someone is behind a prize for bike racing.
explanation.walkthrough: A BAFTA is the British equivalent of an Oscar; 'abaft' is a nautical word.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a sailing term meaning towards or at the stern, so behind.

clue.text: All the same classical things covered by an American writer

indicators.note: something covered by another is wrapped inside it

parts.note: A for an, plus US for American
tho, short for though, means all the same
res is Latin for things

explanation.surface: Classical themes all treated alike by a writer from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: An authoress is a female author, a now old-fashioned word for a woman writer.

clue.text: Censor page?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cover a rude word on air with an electronic tone
second meaning: to summon someone by sending a signal to their pager

explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' suggests a page of a book that needs censoring; it is the verb meaning summon.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both muting swear words with a tone and calling someone on a pager device.

clue.text: Nonsense about exploding fuel bottle? Hardly!

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: bunk is nonsense

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Talk of fuel bottles exploding is dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage; 'Hardly!' says the answer is its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue funk is a state of panic or terror, the very opposite of having bottle.

clue.text: Third rate musical for a rocker?

parts.note: the third grade after A and B
Hair is the 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: A second-rate musical judged by a rock fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocker' suggests a rock fan, but it is a rocking chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocker is a chair on curved runners, so the answer is the broader item.

clue.text: Refund: respond to "I'll scratch yours …"?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a recovery of money already paid out
second meaning: the saying is you scratch my back and I'll scratch yours, so the reply is to scratch back

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is what you do in return for a scratch on the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A clawback is money recovered by a government or company, especially a benefit taken back.

clue.text: Story briefly spread across papers making waves?

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the story goes
spread across means stretched round the outside

parts.note: tale without its last letter
identity papers

explanation.surface: A story in the papers stirring up controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making waves' suggests causing trouble; read literally it describes the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal describes the rise and fall of the sea caused by the moon, producing waves and tides.

clue.text: It's not so acceptable in top class, book being added to wrong set?

indicators.note: being added to means joined onto the end of what follows, so the book goes last

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U usage
the New Testament, a set of books that is the wrong home for an Old Testament book
the Book of Ruth is in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a book added to the wrong set is acceptable among the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage. Ruth belongs in the Old Testament, so adding it to the New Testament puts it in the wrong set.
explanation.definitionFit: An untruth is a statement that is false, something that is not so.

clue.text: Consequence of mounts being placed on piping

indicators.note: in a down clue, being placed on top means coming first in the column

parts.note: mounts and goes up both mean rises; ups are rises
piping hot means very hot

explanation.surface: The result of mounting things onto pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'placed on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot of something is its outcome or final result.

clue.text: Was host of children overheard following me around?

indicators.note: turned around, the word me is read backwards
following means coming after, so the sound-alike part goes second

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: overheard means caught by ear, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: seed means offspring in the Biblical sense

explanation.surface: Someone hosted children who were heard following them around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the sound-alike after the reversed me.
explanation.definitionFit: To emcee is to act as master of ceremonies, hosting an event or show.

clue.text: Swamp ended with tree: crossing hard!

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the pair goes either side of the other letter

parts.note: something ended is over
W is short for with
H for hard, as on pencils
the elm is a tree

explanation.surface: A swamp that finishes with a tree in a hard crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp someone is to overwhelm them, burying them in too much.

clue.text: Extract firm replies from the floor, oddly overlooked

indicators.note: coming up from the floor, in a down clue the letters read bottom to top
overlooking the odd letters means only the even-placed ones are kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Getting firm answers from the audience, though some are odd and ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the floor' suggests audience questions, and 'Extract' a verb; elemi is a resin extracted from trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin obtained from tropical trees, used in varnishes and medicines.

clue.text: With fluorine, no longer having to clean teeth

parts.note: F is the chemical symbol for fluorine
a loss is a state of no longer having something

explanation.surface: Toothpaste fluorine, gone and no longer needed for cleaning teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To floss is to clean between the teeth with thread.

clue.text: Reveals where son's lifted sack?

indicators.note: lifted means picked up and moved higher, here one letter shifts up the column

parts.note: outs means reveals, as in outing a secret
S for son

explanation.surface: Someone reveals where a son stole a sack.
explanation.walkthrough: The son's letter is moved from the end of the word one place higher in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to dismiss them, which is to oust them.

clue.text: Come forth, when expected, by reputation, to retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: estimated time of arrival
a good name is a reputation

explanation.surface: Someone comes forward when expected, then retreats for their reputation's sake.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: Fare, with third deducted, has people wasting tickets?

indicators.note: with its third letter deducted, that letter is taken away

parts.note: nosh is slang for food
owns, with the N removed

explanation.surface: A fare reduced by a third leaves seats unused by ticket holders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price; here it is food, nosh in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: No-shows are people who book or buy tickets but never turn up.

clue.text: Put up with long day — unpleasant conclusion!

parts.note: to stick something is to bear it
to yen for something is to long for it
D for day

explanation.surface: Enduring a long day comes to a grim finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky end is an unpleasant or violent death, a bad conclusion to someone's story.
